# ARS-Codex

This is a Codex adapter for the ARS suite. The vendored ARS content lives under
`ars/`; keep it as source material and route through this file first.

## Versioning

This Codex package is version `0.1.28`. The repo-root `VERSION`, this
`SKILL.md` metadata version, and `manifest.json` `adapter_version` must match.
Vendored ARS suite versions are tracked separately by source repository commit
in `manifest.json`.

## First Rule

Do not load the whole suite by default. Select one workflow, read that workflow's
`WORKFLOW.md`, then load only the agent, reference, template, or shared files needed
for the user's current stage.

The internal workflow entry files are named `WORKFLOW.md`, not `SKILL.md`, so
Codex registers only this root router skill instead of exposing every vendored
upstream workflow as a separate skill.

## Workflow Router

Choose the workflow by intent:

| User intent | Read first |
|---|---|
| Deep research, literature review, systematic review, meta-analysis, fact-checking, research question refinement | `ars/deep-research/WORKFLOW.md` |
| Academic paper writing, paper outline, abstract, revision, citation formatting, AI disclosure, LaTeX/DOCX/PDF formatting guidance | `ars/academic-paper/WORKFLOW.md` |
| Paper review, peer review simulation, editorial decision, reviewer calibration, re-review after revision | `ars/academic-paper-reviewer/WORKFLOW.md` |
| End-to-end research-to-paper pipeline, integrity gate, staged review/revision/finalization workflow | `ars/academic-pipeline/WORKFLOW.md` |
| Experiment planning, code experiment execution plan, human study protocol, statistical interpretation, reproducibility validation | `ars/experiment-agent/WORKFLOW.md` |

If the request spans multiple workflows, start with `ars/academic-pipeline/WORKFLOW.md`
unless the user clearly asked for a single phase.

### Paper Topic Scoping Override

Apply this override before the general paper/pipeline routing rule and before the Claude-Style Alias Router below.
The override applies regardless of whether the user invokes ARS via natural
language or via an `ars-*` alias.

If the user says they want to write a paper, thesis, proposal, article, journal
article, or manuscript, but they only provide a broad topic, tentative title,
research interest, or "??/??/??" and do **not** provide a clear,
answerable research question, route to `ars/deep-research/WORKFLOW.md` in
`socratic` mode first. This matches the upstream ARS experience where vague
paper-topic requests start with SCR/Socratic narrowing instead of immediate
outline or drafting.

Treat these as Socratic triggers even when the wording contains paper-writing
intent:

- "I want to write a paper on ..."
- "I have a paper topic/title ..."
- "???????,???..."
- "????????/??,???????"
- "???????/??????"
- "??? ?? ??? ?? ??? ?? ???? ??"
- "?? ??/?? ??? ??? ??? ???? ????"

First response in this path:

1. State that the request is being routed to `deep-research` `socratic` mode
   because the research question is not yet precise.
2. Ask 3-5 Socratic narrowing questions using `socratic_mentor_agent` and
   `research_question_agent` guidance.
3. Do not produce an outline, draft, literature review, or full pipeline
   dashboard until the user has converged on at least one candidate RQ.

Route directly to `ars/academic-paper/WORKFLOW.md` only when the user already
has a clear RQ, approved study frame, data/results, literature matrix, draft,
or explicitly asks to skip scoping and proceed to outline/drafting. Route to
`ars/academic-pipeline/WORKFLOW.md` only when the user explicitly asks for the
full research-to-paper pipeline or says to continue after Socratic scoping.

## Claude-Style Alias Router

Codex does not install Claude slash commands, but this package emulates their
intent. If the user's request starts with a slash alias (`/ars-plan`) or a plain
alias (`ars-plan`), treat it as a mode shortcut, strip the alias token from the
task text, read the matching `ars/commands/ars-*.md` prompt recipe, then route
to the workflow `WORKFLOW.md` below.

The `model:` field in command frontmatter is a Claude routing hint only. Codex
uses the current model unless the user explicitly requests another model.

| Alias | Read command recipe | Then route to |

| `/ars-plan`, `ars-plan` | `ars/commands/ars-plan.md` | `ars/academic-paper/WORKFLOW.md` in `plan` mode |

| `/ars-mark-read`, `ars-mark-read` | `ars/commands/ars-mark-read.md` | Record a user-attested read declaration against the active Material Passport; every new mark requires a user-owned `read_scope`, with locators allowed only for `sections` scope |
| `/ars-unmark-read`, `ars-unmark-read` | `ars/commands/ars-unmark-read.md` | Rescind a prior human-read mark against the active Material Passport |
| `/ars-cache-invalidate`, `ars-cache-invalidate` | `ars/commands/ars-cache-invalidate.md` | Invalidate cached verification entries for one citation key |
| `/ars-full`, `ars-full` | `ars/commands/ars-full.md` | `ars/academic-pipeline/WORKFLOW.md` |

If the request body after the alias is a vague topic, tentative title, research
direction, or "??/??/??" without a clear research question, defer to the Paper Topic Scoping Override above before routing to the alias's target mode.
This applies to `ars-plan`, `ars-outline`, `ars-abstract`, `ars-lit-review`,
and `ars-full`.

If the Codex client reserves slash-prefixed input before it reaches the model,
tell the user to use the plain alias form, for example `ars-plan my topic`.

## Codex Runtime Mapping

The upstream ARS files were written for Claude Code. Apply these mappings when
using them in Codex:

| Upstream wording | Codex behavior |
|---|---|
| Agent Team, agent, dispatch, handoff | Read the referenced `agents/*.md` file as a role or phase prompt and perform that phase inline. |
| Agent tool, Task tool, subagent | Do not spawn agents automatically. Only use Codex subagents when the user explicitly asks for delegation or parallel agents. If the optional full-runtime profile is enabled, use `codex/full-runtime-manifest.json` and `codex/agents/*.md` as the adapter contract. |
| AskUserQuestion | Ask concise clarification questions, or use Codex's structured user-input tool when available in the active mode. |
| WebSearch | Use Codex web browsing for current facts, source verification, citation checks, and external evidence. Provide source links. |
| Bash, Write, Edit | Treat as capability descriptions, not required tool names. Follow Codex safety rules and the user's filesystem constraints. |
| Agent frontmatter `tools: Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob` | Preserve this as a least-privilege role boundary. The three protected top-level agent roles do not receive Bash or network transport when dispatched separately; inline execution must not use those roles to widen the current task's authority. |
| Claude, Claude Code, model-specific wording | Interpret as "the current Codex agent" unless the text is part of a disclosure template or historical example. |
| `ARS_MODEL_TIERING=economy|quality-boost` | Unset remains the default and preserves current-model behavior. The upstream relative Opus/Sonnet tier names are not hard-mapped to Codex model ids. Apply tiering only when the active Codex runtime supports an explicit per-dispatch model override; otherwise announce a one-line no-op and keep every role on the active model. Use `ars/shared/model_tiering.md` and `ars/scripts/model_tiering_manifest.json` as the classification contract. |
| `ARS_CROSS_MODEL`, `ARS_CROSS_MODEL_REASONING_EFFORT`, `ARS_OPENAI_COMPAT_BASE_URL`, `ARS_OPENAI_COMPAT_API_KEY` | Treat upstream secondary-model dispatch instructions as no-op unless the user explicitly asks for cross-model review. When explicitly enabled in this Codex package, follow `ars/shared/cross_model_verification.md`: identify the provider/model/id status/content class, obtain explicit user consent before any external upload, preserve risk-stratified sampling and blind-disagreement checkpoint rules, and call only the configured provider API. A dispatched owner emits the canonical `[CROSS-MODEL-HANDOFF v1]` envelope; the dispatching Codex context validates it, sends only the payload, applies the mechanical result routing, and returns judgment work to the owner. In reviewer `full` mode, the consented cross-model track swaps the existing Reviewer 2 seat rather than adding a reviewer; re-review runs the independent Priority-1 judge pass and records the Judge Record. Disclose single-family or fallback execution and never simulate either track through the active Codex model. |
| `ARS_CROSS_MODEL_TRANSPORT=codex`, `scripts/cross_model_codex_transport.py` | This explicit selector is limited to contained, one-reference citation checks at Stage 2.5 / 4.5 through a ChatGPT-subscription Codex app-server. Require Codex CLI 0.147.0 or newer, `ARS_CROSS_MODEL`, the exact `Logged in using ChatGPT` attestation on stdout or stderr, and the normal provider/content/cost consent gate; do not accept caller-authored prompts or paths, widen the selector to reviewer/DA/calibration/re-review/handoff calls, or fall back automatically to an API. The provider schema omits unsupported `uniqueItems`, but local validation still rejects duplicate sources. Keep `code_mode` disabled while allowing the bounded search host required by the standalone search tool; the closed event allowlist remains authoritative. A result is accepted only after `turn/completed`, clean process exit, and stdout/stderr EOF; late forbidden or malformed events, drain timeout, nonzero exit, reader failure, or stderr overflow fail visibly. |
| `S2_API_KEY`, `OPENALEX_API_KEY`, `OPENALEX_POLITE_EMAIL`, `CROSSREF_POLITE_EMAIL` | These are optional upstream bibliographic lookup settings. Use them only when the user explicitly runs contamination-signal migration or programmatic reference verification; normal Codex routing does not require them. Never log credential-bearing query strings, and do not use browser retrieval to bypass API rate limits. |
| `ARS_VERIFICATION_CACHE_PATH`, `ARS_CACHE_STALE_ADVISORY_DAYS`, `ARS_CACHE_REVALIDATE` | These configure the local SQLite citation-verification cache, the advisory-only stale-row threshold (default 30 days; `0` disables), and opt-in live re-validation. Preserve cached-by-default behavior when the programmatic citation gate is run. Live re-validation may call external bibliographic services, so use it only within the user's verification task and normal network/credential boundaries; an advisory never becomes a gate failure. |
| Local PDF page anchors, `scripts/pdf_read_preflight.py` | Before trusting a `page` anchor from a locally read PDF, run the structural preflight once and carry its sidecar by `ref_slug`. Treat `FAIL` as positive read-integrity evidence against the page anchor and `UNAVAILABLE` as an explicit advisory; never convert a missing dependency, encrypted file, parser repair, or absent sidecar into `PASS`. The v3.20 `--classify-content` extension is opt-in and process-isolated, depends on the separately pinned `requirements-pdf-content-classifier.txt`, and emits only a `TEXT_AVAILABLE` / `OCR_RECOMMENDED` / `unavailable` advisory while the verdict scope remains `STRUCTURE_ONLY`; never turn it into an automatic OCR or anchor-acceptance gate. |
| `scripts/research_workflow_profile.py` | Treat research-workflow profiles as a deterministic, default-off substrate, not an automatic router. Use only an explicit selection or the visible `field_general` fallback; never infer a research family from the manuscript. Corrections append receipts and mark prior-profile outputs stale without rewriting scholar-owned artifacts. |
| `ARS_INQUIRY_LEDGER=1`, `scripts/inquiry_branch_ledger.py` | The inquiry branch ledger is an opt-in local alpha. When explicitly active, preserve author-owned append events, bounded summaries, project/path identity, locking, recovery, and individually visible stale causes. The flag authorizes no external model, API, or search call and yields no novelty, correctness, value, or usability claim. |
| `scripts/check_promotion_bakeoff_preregistration.py` | Preserve the sealed commitment/reveal contracts and use the hermetic unit tests in this package. Do not run direct `verify-tree` against the re-rooted vendored subtree: it intentionally lacks the complete canonical upstream Git history required by that release-discipline check. A real future bakeoff must run from the upstream repository and still requires explicit consent for every live model call and cost. |
| `fresh Claude Code session`, `Claude Code session` | Read as "a new Codex conversation". Material Passport reset semantics still apply; only the runtime changes. This rule covers `ars/academic-pipeline/WORKFLOW.md`, `ars/academic-pipeline/agents/pipeline_orchestrator_agent.md`, `ars/academic-pipeline/references/passport_as_reset_boundary.md`, `ars/experiment-agent/README.md`, `ars/experiment-agent/README.zh-TW.md`, and `ars/docs/PERFORMANCE.md`. |
| `/ars-*` slash command, Claude plugin command | Treat `ars/commands/ars-*.md` as optional prompt recipes. Codex does not register slash commands from this package. |
| SessionStart hook, SubagentStop hook, `hooks/hooks.json`, `scripts/ars_update_check.sh` | Treat as upstream Claude Code hook metadata only. The v3.18 update checker is vendored for traceability and tests but is not installed or executed by Codex; Codex package updates remain manual unless the user explicitly asks to port hook behavior. |

### Bibliographic Network Routing

The upstream prompt contracts, Python resolver clients, and v3.21
claim-standing adapters are distinct execution paths. Apply this table before
following any vendored instruction that says a lookup happens automatically:

| Path | Default ARS-Codex behavior | Dedicated client trigger |
|---|---|---|
| Ordinary topic or candidate discovery | Use Codex browsing and authoritative web sources. | Never launches the Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, Crossref, or arXiv Python resolver clients. |
| Agent-side ingest, deduplication, and source verification | In the default inline route, translate prompt-level `WebSearch` or index lookups into Codex browsing or official metadata pages. | Upstream prompt wording such as "automatic S2 lookup" does not itself launch a Python client in Codex. |
| Script-backed citation-existence gate | Do not infer this from an `ars-full` request alone. Stage 2.5 and 4.5 remain mandatory integrity checkpoints, but default Codex routing performs their source work through browsing unless the user also requests programmatic verification. | An explicit request to run `verify_passport.py`, `verification_gate`, or equivalent programmatic reference verification. Once invoked, cache misses may call Crossref, OpenAlex, and Semantic Scholar for non-manual references; arXiv runs only when `arxiv_id` is present. Manual references skip all four. |
| Claim-standing discovery | Offer only after an eligible Claim Registry row at Stage 2.5 or 4.5. It is advisory and separate from citation verification. | A separate user request plus affirmative, plan-bound consent. It uses the v3.21 keyword-discovery adapters, not the four single-reference resolver clients; absent, cancelled, invalidated, or stale consent means no call. |
| Contamination backfill or migration | No automatic migration. | Only the explicitly selected migration CLI and its documented indexes. |

The canonical upstream network map remains available at
`ars/docs/DATA_FLOWS.md`; this section is the Codex adapter override for when
those flows are actually launched here.

### ARS v3.21.1 Contract-Honesty Boundaries

- Phase E evidence rows are deterministic, source-bound checkpoint artifacts.
  They preserve the existing citation verdict and gate, do not mark a source as
  human-read, and must replay against explicit session-held source bytes.
- Revision roadmaps remain non-ranking proposals. Only an explicit author
  adjudication may authorize exact choices or integrity-correction targets;
  never infer, fabricate, or auto-apply author decisions. Optional cross-run
  adjudication-activity capture is local, best-effort, and advisory only.
- Review-target context must be author-confirmed, and criteria are carried by
  resolved pointers across formative, internal, and external review. Do not
  infer a missing venue/track, invent evidence, or let binding conformance alter
  integrity verdicts, editorial arithmetic, checkpoints, or author triage.
- Human-subjects authority resolution keeps review-ethics and data-protection
  axes separate and fails closed when scope, currency, or applicability is
  unresolved. Outputs remain institution-owned navigation aids, never legal
  advice, an IRB/REC determination, an authorization, or a fabricated timeline.

28:{"round": "S1/open", "candidate": "astra_1", "prior": "KNOWN", "refs": ["https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.08076 (Tian, Eriksson, Vitos 2020, pressure effect on order-disorder in L1_0 FeNi, doi:10.1038/s41598-020-71551-4)", "https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.0622 (Geng, Chen, Sluiter, PRB 70 094203, fcc Ni-Al phase stability under pressure)", "https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.0646 (Geng, Sluiter, Chen, PRB 72 014204, order-disorder effects on EOS in fcc Ni-Al)", "volume-dependent ECIs, Alling/Ruban 2011, already logged in ledger 0dffc5bf40"], "verdict": "DROP", "why": "The arithmetic checks out. data/r3b_l12.csv:30 gives E_ord +1.49 meV and S_ord +231.6 meV. Recomputing with the h1 grid points emix_2 and emix_4 at lnV -0.030 and +0.030 gives about +1.40 and +214, and -S_ord/V0 = -2.91 GPa. The Co3Ir control (row 21: -41.5 meV, slope 259) also matches. But this is not a regularity. It is a linear extrapolation of two numbers for one compound: any cell with E_ord near 0 and a nonzero ordering slope crosses zero at t = -E_ord/S_ord. Ni3Ir and Co3Ir have the same slope sign and similar size, so the only real contrast is E_ord(V0). Volume-dependent cluster expansion and the pressure-dependent ordering literature already give this, and the candidate admits CE can represent it. The 1.4 meV signal is below noise. It comes from a single seed=0 108-atom random cell. For equiatomic Ni-Ir, seeds 0/1/2 give E_mix -190.9/-192.4/-178.9 meV (13.5 meV spread) and slopes spread about 85 meV per unit lnV (data/h1_ev_rows_fixed.csv, data/binary_seeds.csv), so the crossing at t = -0.0065 is not resolved. MACE's MAE on ordered-cell energies vs PBE is 7.0 meV (ledger 7e0ff785d1), so even the sign at V0 is outside L1 accuracy. Ni magnetism is not separated out. Clamped equal-volume energies are also the wrong thermodynamic comparison under pressure. Letting each phase relax to its own volume already lowers E_ord by about S_ord^2/(2BV), roughly 1.3 meV at B about 230 GPa. So at P=0 the two phases are degenerate within that correction, and the real test would be dH(P), not dE at fixed t. Nothing here tests or corrects a mechanical-property formula."}

All three fixed predictions reproduce exactly from 1.5*K50(V) - K(complement). But r(1-x) = -r(x) is the subregular first Redlich-Kister term, a known form. It also does not answer the front. (a) It does not single out one channel: the same rows carry nearly equal K44 and Kp residuals, and Kp still transfers with gain 0.55. (b) It is not specific to Co. The largest 25/75 binary residuals include Cu-Rh +6.7/+7.6, Cu-Ir -5.7, Au-Ir -5.2 and Au-Rh -4.6, while the K44 residual is under 1 GPa for Co-Ni, Co-Cu, Ag-Co and Au-Co. (c) Each fixed prediction inherits the seed-0 error of the old row. K44 seed SD at V_ij is 2.1 to 2.4 GPa for Co-Ir, Co-Pt and Cu-Pt (seed-0 Cu-Pt 50:50 alone sits -2.4 from the mean), the tolerances are 2.5 to 3, and no power was computed, so a true hypothesis would often fail. (d) The L1 term vanishes for any pair with x_i = x_j, so in multicomponent alloys it only matters for strongly off-equiatomic pairs. It could come back as a subregular extension of the rule covering both channels, but not as the explanation for K44."}

48:{"time": "2026-11-01T00:32:50", "candidate": "K' shear-curvature volume transfer (L2 697c2d6d75), Marker 2017 full text (accepted manuscript, 45 pp, read in full)", "prior": "DIFFERENT: Marker is our own-volume Muggianu baseline", "refs": ["Marker, Shang, Zhao, Liu, Comput Mater Sci 140 121 (2017), doi 10.1016/j.commatsci.2017.08.037", "Liu, Zhang, Ganeshan, Wang, Mathaudhu, Scr Mater 63 686 (2010): origin of CALPHAD modelling of c_ij (Marker ref 25)"], "verdict": "KEEP", "why": "Eq 14: c_ij(x) = sum x_A c_A + sum x_A x_B [L0 + L1 (x_A - x_B)] + sum x_A x_B x_C L2, fitted separately to C11, C12, C44 (not C') of fully relaxed PBE SQS (16-64 atoms), bcc Ti-X-Y (X,Y = Mo, Nb, Sn, Ta, Zr). Every input is at its own equilibrium volume; no volume or strain dependence of L anywhere; no excess/clamped decomposition. Only Ti-X binaries exist, so X0.5Y0.5 ends are off (e.g. Nb-Zr, Mo-Zr C11 and C44 by 20-40 GPa), which they attribute to missing non-Ti binaries; ternary L2 hardly helps (Janz-Schmid-Fetzer). # Academic Paper Reviewer v1.11.1 - Multi-Perspective Academic Paper Review Agent Team

Simulates a complete international journal peer review process: automatically identifies the paper's field, dynamically configures 4 card-backed identities (Journal-Fit Reviewer + 3 peer reviewers), and adds the fixed Devil's Advocate as the fifth execution seat. The five role-separated perspectives cover journal fit, methodology, domain expertise, cross-disciplinary viewpoints, and core argument challenges; a separate editorial synthesizer produces the structured Editorial Decision and Revision Roadmap.

**v1.1 Improvements**:
1. Added Devil's Advocate Reviewer - specifically challenges core arguments, detects logical fallacies, and identifies the strongest counter-arguments
2. Added `re-review` mode - verification review, focused on checking whether revisions address the review comments
3. Expanded review team from 4 to 5 members

> **Routing discipline (v3.9.2):** see `.claude/CLAUDE.md` "Routing Discipline (v3.9.2)" + `shared/references/intent_clarification_protocol.md` for cross-skill routing rules. This skill assumes routing has already settled - ambiguous cross-phase materials should have been clarified upstream.

---

## Quick Start

**Simplest command:**
```
Review this paper: [paste paper or provide file]
```

**Output:**
1. Automatically identifies the paper's field and methodology type
2. Dynamically configures four card-backed reviewer identities; the fixed Devil's Advocate is the fifth execution seat
3. 5 role-separated review reports (4 configuration cards plus the fixed Devil's Advocate, with typed execution provenance)
4. 1 Editorial Decision Letter + Revision Roadmap

---

## Trigger Conditions

### Trigger Keywords

**English**: review paper, peer review, manuscript review, referee report, review my paper, critique paper, simulate review, editorial review, calibrate reviewer, reviewer calibration, measure reviewer accuracy

**???**: ?? ??, ?? ??, ?? ??, ?? ??, ?? ???, ??? ???? ??, ??? ??, ?? ??? ??

**????**: ????, ????, ????, ????, ?????, ????????, ?????

### Non-Trigger Scenarios

| Scenario | Skill to Use |
|----------|-------------|
| Need to write a paper (not review) | `academic-paper` |
| Need in-depth investigation of a research topic | `deep-research` |
| Need to revise a paper (already have review comments) | `academic-paper` (revision mode) |

### Quick Mode Selection Guide

| Your Situation | Recommended Mode | Spectrum |
|----------------|-----------------|----------|
| Need comprehensive review (first submission) | full | balanced |
| Checking if revisions addressed comments | re-review | fidelity |
| Quick quality assessment (15 min) | quick | fidelity |
| Focus only on methods/statistics | methodology-focus | fidelity |
| Want to learn by doing (guided review) | guided | originality |
| Want to measure this reviewer's bounded decision-error profile on an adjudicated target set | calibration | fidelity |

**Spectrum** (v3.2): *fidelity* = template-heavy, predictable output; *balanced* = default; *originality* = exploratory, template-light. See `shared/mode_spectrum.md` for the full cross-skill spectrum table.

Not sure? Use `full` for pre-submission review, `re-review` for post-revision verification. Current live reviews and Schema 6 packages declare `NOT_CALIBRATED`; a full-tier calibration run may produce a bounded candidate profile, but live-profile application remains unavailable until its closed artifact and replay validator ship. `calibration` is opt-in: its default full tier measures bounded decision-level FNR/FPR, while the explicitly selected 3-paper directional tier gives only a low-cost Minor/Major boundary signal and remains `NOT_CALIBRATED`.

---

## Agent Team (7 Agents)

| # | Agent | Role | Phase |
|---|-------|------|-------|
| 1 | `field_analyst_agent` | Analyzes the paper's field and dynamically configures 4 card-backed identities; the Devil's Advocate remains a fixed fifth seat | Phase 0 |
| 2 | `eic_agent` | Journal-Fit Reviewer - journal fit, originality, overall quality; one panel card, no final-decision authority | Phase 1 |
| 3 | `methodology_reviewer_agent` | Peer Reviewer 1 - research design, statistical validity, reproducibility | Phase 1 |
| 4 | `domain_reviewer_agent` | Peer Reviewer 2 - literature coverage, theoretical framework, domain contribution | Phase 1 |
| 5 | `perspective_reviewer_agent` | Peer Reviewer 3 - cross-disciplinary connections, practical impact, challenging fundamental assumptions | Phase 1 |
| 6 | **`devils_advocate_reviewer_agent`** | **Devil's Advocate - core argument challenges, logical fallacy detection, strongest counter-arguments** | **Phase 1** |
| 7 | `editorial_synthesizer_agent` | Synthesizes all reviews, identifies consensus and disagreements, makes editorial decision | Phase 2 |

**Role-name compatibility (#611):** the public display name is **Journal-Fit Reviewer**. The stable implementation identifiers remain `eic_agent` (agent), `eic` (`contract_role` / dispatch role), and `EIC` (serialized reviewer/source ID, including `EIC-W<n>`). Those compatibility tokens do not select a Stage 3' agent file: `editorial_synthesizer_agent` emits first-round decisions, while contract-governed re-review uses its three dedicated calls and checker-derived outcome.

---

## Orchestration Workflow (3 Phases)

```
User: "Review this paper"
     |
=== Phase 0: FIELD ANALYSIS & PERSONA CONFIGURATION ===
     |
     +-> [field_analyst_agent] -> Reviewer Configuration Card (x4)
         - Reads the complete paper
         - Identifies: primary discipline, secondary discipline, research paradigm, methodology type, target journal tier, paper maturity
         - Dynamically generates specific identities for 4 card-backed reviewers:
           * Journal-Fit Reviewer (internal `EIC`): which journal/editor perspective, area of expertise, review preferences
           * Reviewer 1 (Methodology): Methodological expertise, what they particularly focus on
           * Reviewer 2 (Domain): Domain expertise, research interests
           * Reviewer 3 (Perspective): Cross-disciplinary angle, what unique perspective they bring
         - The fifth execution seat is the fixed Devil's Advocate, which receives no dynamic configuration card
     |
     ** Presents Reviewer Configuration to user for confirmation (adjustable) **
     |
=== Phase 1: PARALLEL MULTI-PERSPECTIVE REVIEW ===
     |
     |-> [eic_agent] -------> Journal-Fit Review Report
     |   - Journal fit, originality, significance, relevance to readership
     |   - Does not go deep into methodology (that's Reviewer 1's job)
     |   - One role-separated card among five - no peer-output channel before commitment (Iron Rule #2)
     |
     |-> [methodology_reviewer_agent] -> Methodology Review Report
     |   - Research design rigor, sampling strategy, data collection
     |   - Analysis method selection, statistical validity, effect sizes
     |   - Reproducibility, data transparency
     |
     |-> [domain_reviewer_agent] -------> Domain Review Report
     |   - Literature review completeness, theoretical framework appropriateness
     |   - Academic argument accuracy, incremental contribution to the field
     |   - Missing key references
     |
     |-> [perspective_reviewer_agent] --> Perspective Review Report
     |   - Cross-disciplinary connections and borrowing opportunities
     |   - Practical applications and policy implications
     |   - Broader social or ethical implications
     |
     +-> [devils_advocate_reviewer_agent] --> Devil's Advocate Report
         - Core argument challenges (strongest counter-arguments)
         - Cherry-picking detection
         - Confirmation bias detection
         - Logic chain validation
         - Overgeneralization detection
         - Alternative paths analysis
         - Stakeholder blind spots
         - "So what?" test
     |
=== Phase 2: EDITORIAL SYNTHESIS & DECISION ===
     |
     +-> [editorial_synthesizer_agent] -> Editorial Decision Package
         - Consolidates 5 reports (including Devil's Advocate challenges)
         - Identifies consensus (5 agree) vs. disagreement (divergent opinions)
         - Arbitration and argumentation for disputed issues
         - Devil's Advocate CRITICAL issues are specially flagged in the Editorial Decision
         - Editorial Decision Letter
         - Immutable non-ranking Revision Roadmap core (directly consumed with a separate explicit author sidecar)
     |
=== Phase 2.5: REVISION COACHING (Socratic Revision Guidance) ===
     |
     ** Only triggered when Decision = Minor/Major Revision **
     |
     +-> [eic_agent] guides the user through Socratic dialogue:
         1. Overall positioning - "After reading the review comments, what surprised you the most?"
         2. Core issue focus - Guides user to understand consensus issues
         3. Contribution framing probe - ask the Layer-5 later-stage anchored forms
            L5-W1 / L5-W2 / L5-W3 (single-sourced under Layer 5 in
            deep-research/agents/socratic_mentor_agent.md - read the question text
            there), anchored to what the manuscript already claims ("the revised
            paper"). Questions only - never propose, substitute, rank, expand, or
            select a contribution claim (Kong L2 verb test); the user answers.
         4. Explicit author triage - records `will_address`, `wont_address`, or `not_on_point` for every source-ordered item, with no inferred work order
         5. Counter-argument response - Guides user to think about how to respond to Devil's Advocate challenges
         6. Implementation planning - confirms exact block/operation scope and any registered-claim or declined-overlap authorization

.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:493:.orchestra/LESSONS.md
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:494:1: # Lessons for derivation agents (Astra, Opus)
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:495:2: 
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:496:3: Read before proposing. Each line is a way a candidate died or nearly died for the wrong reason. Updated 2026-10-31.
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:497:4: 
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:498:5: 1. Ratios of energies blow up where the denominator crosses zero (R3: n_eff = -3 b/a reached -102 for Cu-Ir). Prefer
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:499:6:    predictions linear in measured quantities; if a ratio is essential, say where it is undefined.
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:500:7: 2. Compare like with like: clamped with clamped, relaxed with relaxed, random with random. R3 compared a relaxed random
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:501:8:    volume with a clamped L1_0 volume; even the exact formula then had slope 0.20.
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:502:9: 3. Ordered cells are not random alloys. In PBE, 4-atom ordered cells carry a fixed-volume many-body term (~10 meV/atom)
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:503:10:    that random alloys lack. A random-alloy rule must be tested on random (SQS) cells.
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:504:11: 4. If your rule's main content is a common shift, a test with a free intercept cannot see it. State the test you expect
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:505:12:    to pass, and check its power by simulation (harness/power.py) before data exist.
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:506:13: 5. Results that survived so far: volume transfer of binary interactions (L2, refit k = 0.79 on both holdouts, not
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:507:14:    input noise); isotropic chemical shear softening K44 ~ K' in Ir/Rh alloys (MACE, PBE pending). Build on these.
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:508:15: 6. Results that died for real: A2 (shear from hydrostatic derivatives; even a free 2-term fit has r 0.37), H-sm
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:509:16:    (predicted K44/K' = 4, measured 1.05), R3b (exponent sharing). Do not resubmit without a new mechanism.
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:510:17: 7. PBE: pure references must share the alloy's cutoff (dft.Settings(ecut_elements=...)). Earlier PBE mixing numbers
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:511:18:    carry a cutoff mismatch; its size is being measured (data/ecut_bias.csv).
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:512:19: 8. Round R1 (Astra and Opus independently): 108-atom cells round atom counts, but references used nominal fractions,
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:513:20:    so every non-integer composition carried up to ~60 meV/atom of bookkeeping error. Fixed in data/*_fixed.csv
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:514:21:    (column comp_actual is the real composition) and in the generators. Always reference the composition the cell has.
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:515:22: 9. PBE cutoff mismatch corrected (harness/ecutfix.py, validated to 0.002 meV/atom). MACE now PASSES L1 for the
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:516:23:    ordered-cell beyond-pair Delta (sign 9/10, r 0.80); PBE quaternary Delta +12.9 meV is real. MACE data on ordered
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:517:24:    multicomponent cells can be used.
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:518:25: 10. Round R2 (Astra): the arena's permutation count capped the smallest reachable p at 1/501, so after five tests no
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:519:26:     candidate could pass however good it was. Fixed: n_perm grows with m. Also open: generators set V0 from nominal
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:520:27:     fractions while comp_actual differs (~0.5% in volume, ~0.06 meV RMSE effect, not the cause of k ~ 0.8).
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:521:28: 11. k ~ 0.8 was mostly linearisation: E_ij(V) is strongly nonlinear over |ln(V0/V_ij)| up to 0.36. Exact binary
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:522:29:     energies at the alloy volume give k 0.94 [0.90, 0.98] and RMSE 10.3 meV with no parameter (data/binary_vgrid.csv).
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:523:30: 12. Swarm S1 audit (Astra): (a) scripts/hiso_l12.py did not use ecut_elements, and harness/dft.py picks the k-grid
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:524:31:     from the strained cell (18x18x18 vs 17x18x18), so 0.1 meV/atom of strain-dependent error moves K by 1.6 to 4.7
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:525:32:     GPa. H-iso results before the fix are not evidence either way; the run is stopped. (b) fix_counts.py treated
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:526:33:     0.3333 as the reference weight of equiatomic ternaries (36+36+36 atoms are exact): +0.3 to +0.7 meV added.
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:527:34:     (c) B_chem and R in *_fixed.csv are stale. (d) K44 ~ K' is not Zener invariance.
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:528:35: 13. k at fixed composition (h1/h3 E(V) curves vs exact binary response): 0.976 [0.956, 1.001]. No reduced volume
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:529:36:     response; k ~ 0.8 is the curvature the linear transfer leaves out (94% of the shift).
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:530:37: 
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:531:38: 14. Shear-curvature volume transfer (prereg 4c29d9754c, result 6e0923b413), 113 unseen h3 alloys, binary curvatures
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:532:39:     at the alloy volume, no parameter. Kp: 4.77 -> 2.03 GPa, gain 0.57, p 2.5e-4, refit k 1.08 (pass). K44: 3.29 -> 2.62,
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:533:40:     gain 0.20, p 0.023, refit k 0.86 (fail at p < 0.005). Joint claim FAIL. The first design (sigma = pair-sum residual,
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:534:41:     which contains the signal) had power 0.45 and was stopped before any target existed. K44's worst rule errors are
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:535:42:     Co-rich (Co ~0.46 with Pt or Cu), where the rule is worse than no transfer; cause not yet audited (hypothesis,
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:536:43:     design or numerics). Do not re-split the joint claim after the fact: a K44 or Kp claim needs its own fresh test.
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:537:44: 
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:538:45: 15. K' alone, fresh blind test (prereg 67a358fc59, result d92844787f, L2 entry recorded): 94 hm_fresh alloys, K' 4.22 ->
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:539:46:     1.89 GPa, gain 0.55, p 2.5e-4, refit k 1.08, 75/94 better. Two independent blind sets now agree for K' (k 1.08 both).
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:540:47:     K44 again weaker (gain 0.12, k 0.69, not gated). Why K44 transfers worse than K' is open: Co-rich outliers, or
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:541:48:     internal (non-affine) relaxation channels that the clamped protocol suppresses differently for the two shears.
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:542:49: 
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:543:50: 16. Model swap of the K' rule (prereg 851aec6883, result 86767e478d): medium-mpa-0, same geometry, same 94 hm_fresh
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:544:51:     alloys, binaries seed 0 only. K' 4.73 -> 2.28 GPa, gain 0.52, p 2.5e-4, but refit k 1.33 [1.11, 1.51]: the
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:545:52:     pre-registered k-contains-1 condition FAILS. K44 gain 0.16, k 0.77. Reading: that the alloy's K' follows the binaries
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:546:53:     at the alloy volume and cuts the error in half survives a model with a different shear bias; that the coefficient is
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:547:54:     exactly 1 does not (omat 1.08 twice, mpa 1.33). Binary seed noise would pull k down, not up. The two models disagree
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:548:55:     most at |dlnV| > 0.2 (K' corr 0.80 vs 0.96 within 0.1). Cause not yet audited. Do not claim "parameter-free" across
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:549:56:     models; the PBE check decides which k is physical.
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:550:57: 
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:551:58: 17. K44 transfer fails only with Co (prereg e410c96a32, result d9460850ce). 120 fresh Co-free alloys: K44 pair 4.68 ->
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:552:59:     rule 2.30 GPa, gain 0.51, p 2.5e-4, k 1.23 (PASS). 60 fresh alloys with Co >= 15%: gain 0.11, p 0.08, k 0.70. K'
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:553:60:     passes in both. Open confound: the Co-free set has a larger volume signal (pair error 4.68 vs 3.36), so "Co breaks
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:554:61:     K44" and "K44 needs a large signal" are not yet separated; match the two sets on |rule - pair| before claiming
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:555:62:     a Co mechanism (magnetism is a guess, MACE has no spin).
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:556:63:     Confound check (exploratory, same fresh rows, tertiles of |rule - pair|): at matched signal Co-free gain 0.37 / 0.58
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:557:64:     vs Co 0.08 / 0.22 (mid / large), and Co alloys carry a larger floor at small signal (rule rms 2.61 vs 1.73 GPa).
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:558:65:     The Co effect survives signal matching; not yet a registered claim.
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:559:66: 
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:560:67: 18. Why K44 looked broken (Opus, swarm S2, blind by file timestamp, confirmed on 60 Co alloys). The part the pair rule
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:561:68:     misses is the same in both shears (corr 0.71, slope ~1). K44's volume signal is half of K''s, so the shared floor
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:562:69:     swamps it; in Co alloys the floor anticorrelates with the signal and drags k to 0.7. Remove the floor (A = K44 - K'
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:563:70:     or e' as covariate) and K44 transfers with k ~1. LESSONS 14-16 failure reason: design, not hypothesis.
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:564:71: 
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:565:72: 19. Shared SQS seed leak (Opus S2 audit, Astra confirmed). compute.py:56 draws the site permutation from (seed, n)
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:566:73:     only, so every seed-0 cell thresholds one random field: seed-0 targets and seed-0 binaries share configuration
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:567:74:     noise. K' is immune (gain 0.55-0.58, k 1.07-1.10 for every seed split). K44 is not: leak-free gain 0.06-0.14,
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:568:75:     k 0.60-0.77. d9460850ce and the LESSONS 18 Co check used the leak; 9cfc8edaf0 was withdrawn before reading and
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:569:76:     re-registered as c2eff007ad with target seed 100. Rule: targets and inputs never share a seed.
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:570:77: 
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:571:78: 20. Shared floor, disjoint seeds (c2eff007ad -> b86e0d8a40 PASS, 150 alloys): A = K44 - K' transfers (gain 0.49),
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:572:79:     corr(e44, e') 0.77, joint k 0.91, b 0.94; plain K44 Co-free gain 0.47, Co 0.09. Astra audit: PLAUSIBLE, the
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:573:80:     null could not separate a compositional floor from same-cell noise. A shared-channel claim needs targets for the
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:574:81:     two channels from different cells. Test fd786169e3.
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:575:82: 
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:576:83: 21. The shared floor is compositional (fd786169e3 PASS, two cells per composition, unique seeds): cross-cell corr
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:577:84:     0.75 vs same-cell 0.79, k 0.92, b 0.95; Astra audit PLAUSIBLE (cell noise ~5% of the shared covariance). Next
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:578:85:     doubt is a known identity: clamped curvatures carry the initial stress, K44 = C44 + s_yy, K' = C' + (s_xx+s_yy)/2.
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:579:86:     A floor claim must survive subtracting it (k_floor_stress.py). Pre-register every step; one audit, one test.
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:580:

.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:976:36: def site_counts(comp: dict[str, float], n: int) -> dict[str, int]:
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:977:37:     counts = {el: int(round(x * n)) for el, x in comp.items()}
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:978:38:     counts[max(counts, key=counts.get)] += n - sum(counts.values())
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:979:39:     return counts

.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:982:42: def actual_fractions(atoms: Atoms) -> dict[str, float]:
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:983:43:     """Composition the cell really has. Subtract pure references with these, not the nominal fractions (the
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:984:44:     rounding to whole atoms shifted E_mix by up to ~57 meV/atom before 2026-10-31)."""
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:985:45:     s = atoms.get_chemical_symbols()
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:986:46:     return {el: s.count(el) / len(s) for el in sorted(set(s))}
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:987:47: 
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:988:48: 
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:989:49: def solid_solution(comp: dict[str, float], lattice: str, reps: int, seed: int) -> Atoms:
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:990:50:     """Random solid solution on a cubic conventional supercell (no SQS optimisation). Counts are rounded to whole
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:991:51:     atoms; use actual_fractions() for references."""
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:992:52:     a = sum(x * A0[lattice].get(el, 3.5 if lattice == "fcc" else 3.1) for el, x in comp.items())
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:993:53:     atoms = bulk("X", lattice, a=a, cubic=True).repeat((reps, reps, reps))
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:994:54:     counts = site_counts(comp, len(atoms))
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:995:55:     symbols = [el for el, c in counts.items() for _ in range(c)]
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:996:56:     np.random.default_rng(seed).shuffle(symbols)
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:997:57:     atoms.set_chemical_symbols(symbols)
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:998:58:     return atoms
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:999:59: 
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1000:60: 
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1001:61: # GPU duty cycle in (0, 1]: after each relaxation sleep so the GPU is busy only this fraction
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1002:62: # of the time. Keeps a laptop from overheating on long scans; results are unaffected.
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1003:63: DUTY = float(os.environ.get("HARNESS_DUTY", "1.0"))

.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1009:69:     opt = FIRE(target, logfile=None)
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1010:70:     t = time.perf_counter()
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1011:71:     opt.run(fmax=fmax, steps=steps)
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1012:72:     if DUTY < 1:
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1013:73:         time.sleep((time.perf_counter() - t) * (1 / DUTY - 1))
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1014:74:     return opt.nsteps

.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1017:77: def elastic_tensor(atoms: Atoms, eps: float = 0.005, relax_ions: bool = True) -> np.ndarray:
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1018:78:     """Full 6x6 Voigt tensor (GPa) from central differences of stress, ions relaxed at each strain."""
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1019:79:     cell0 = atoms.get_cell().array.copy()
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1020:80:     C = np.zeros((6, 6))
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1021:81:     voigt = [(0, 0), (1, 1), (2, 2), (1, 2), (0, 2), (0, 1)]
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1022:82:     for j, (k, l) in enumerate(voigt):
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1023:83:         sig = []
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1024:84:         for s in (+eps, -eps):
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1025:85:             e = np.zeros((3, 3))
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1026:86:             if k == l:
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1027:87:                 e[k, k] = s
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1028:88:             else:
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1029:89:                 e[k, l] = e[l, k] = s / 2  # engineering shear strain = s
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1030:90:             strained = atoms.copy()
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1031:91:             strained.set_cell(cell0 @ (np.eye(3) + e), scale_atoms=True)
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1032:92:             strained.calc = calculator()
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1033:93:             if relax_ions and len(strained) > 1:
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1034:94:                 relax(strained, cell=False, fmax=5e-4)
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1035:95:             sig.append(strained.get_stress(voigt=True) * GPA)  # ASE: tensile stress positive
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1036:96:         C[:, j] = (sig[0] - sig[1]) / (2 * eps)
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1037:97:     return 0.5 * (C + C.T)

.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1042:1: """Power check for a pre-registered test, run before the test data exist.
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1043:2: 
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1044:3: A test is only informative if (a) data generated with the hypothesis TRUE, at realistic noise, pass it most of the
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1045:4: time and (b) data with the hypothesis FALSE rarely pass. Both are estimated by simulation. Two failures this tool is
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1046:5: meant to catch, from 2026-10-31: the L3 ordered-cell design (an intercept absorbed the rule's main signal) and R3
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1047:6: (the observable compared relaxed with clamped volumes, so even the exact formula had slope 0.20).
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1048:7: """
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1049:8: 
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1050:9: from __future__ import annotations
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1051:10: 
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1052:11: from typing import Callable
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1053:12: 
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1054:13: import numpy as np
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1055:14: 
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1056:15: 
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1057:16: def power(test: Callable[[object], bool], simulate_true: Callable[[np.random.Generator], object],
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1058:17:           simulate_null: Callable[[np.random.Generator], object], n: int = 300, seed: int = 0) -> dict:
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1059:18:     rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1060:19:     p = np.mean([bool(test(simulate_true(rng))) for _ in range(n)])
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1061:20:     f = np.mean([bool(test(simulate_null(rng))) for _ in range(n)])
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1062:21:     return {"power": round(float(p), 3), "false_pass": round(float(f), 3), "n_sims": n}
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1063:22:

.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1065:24: def near_zero_divisor(x, name: str, frac: float = 0.1) -> list[int]:
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1066:25:     """Indices where a quantity used as a divisor is small relative to its spread (ratio predictions blow up there)."""
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1067:26:     x = np.asarray(x, dtype=float)
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1068:27:     bad = np.flatnonzero(np.abs(x) < frac * np.std(x))
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1069:28:     if len(bad):
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1070:29:         print(f"warning: {name} near zero at rows {bad.tolist()}; a ratio-based prediction is unstable there")
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1071:30:     return bad.tolist()

1:"""Fresh test of the shared-floor picture of shear transfer (LESSONS 18; Opus, swarm S2 k44 front).

3:python scripts/k_aniso_fresh.py
4:Seen so far (k44_cofree Co set, blind by file timestamp only): the residual of the volume-transfer pair rule is the
5:same in both shears, so the anisotropy A = K44 - K' transfers as sum 4 x_i x_j A_ij(V0) and K44 transfers with k ~1
6:once e' = K' - rule' is a covariate. Here both are pre-registered in the ledger on 150 new random alloys (half with
7:Co >= 15%), drawn with a new seed and never computed. Targets use SQS seed 100: binaries use seeds 0-2, and compute.py:56
8:makes the site permutation depend only on (seed, n), so a shared seed leaks configuration noise (S2 audit, ledger
9:withdrawal of 9cfc8edaf0). Plain K44 per Co set is reported, not gated.
10:PASS needs all three: (1) A rule: RMSE <= 0.9 x pair-at-V_ij and sign-flip p < 0.005; (2) corr(e44, e') >= 0.5;
11:(3) joint fit K44 - pair44 = k T44 + b e': k and b both in [0.7, 1.3].

48:- Interpolation or clamped/single-seed results are estimates, not direct pressure/ordering evidence. For small crossings such as Ni3Ir, compare signal to random-cell seed scatter and use enthalpy rather than fixed-volume energies. [Task 2]

1:"""Correct the reference error found by Astra in round R1: compute.solid_solution rounds atom counts to the 108-site
2:cell, but E_mix subtracted pure energies with the nominal fractions x. The logged value is
3:    E_logged(V) = E_mix(x~, V) + sum_i (x~_i - x_i) e_i(V),   x~_i = N_i / 108.
4:We remove the second term (MACE pure fcc energies at the same V) and keep the actual composition x~ in comp_actual.
5:
6:python scripts/fix_counts.py
7:Writes *_fixed.csv next to each input; sealed hm3 is corrected in place of its sealed copy (hm3fix), unread.
8:"""
9:
10:import os
11:import sys
12:from pathlib import Path
13:
14:ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
15:os.environ["HARNESS_MODEL"] = "medium-omat-0"
16:sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
17:
18:import numpy as np  # noqa: E402
19:import pandas as pd  # noqa: E402
20:from ase.build import bulk  # noqa: E402
21:
22:from harness import arena, compute  # noqa: E402
23:from harness.fcc_set import key  # noqa: E402
24:from harness.features import parse_comp  # noqa: E402
25:
26:N = 108
27:SCALES = np.linspace(0.97, 1.03, 7)
28:pv = pd.read_csv(ROOT / "data" / "scan_fcc_omat_pure.csv").set_index("el")["vol_per_atom"]
29:calc = compute.calculator()
30:_pe = {}
31:
32:
33:from harness.fcc_set import compositions, fresh_compositions  # noqa: E402
34:
35:# tie-break in compute.solid_solution follows the generator's dict order (equiatomic rows), so recover that order
36:ORDER = {key(c): list(c) for c in list(compositions()) + list(fresh_compositions())}
37:
38:
39:def actual(comp):
40:    comp = {e: comp[e] for e in ORDER.get(key(comp), list(comp))}
41:    counts = {el: int(round(x * N)) for el, x in comp.items()}  # same rule as compute.solid_solution
42:    counts[max(counts, key=counts.get)] += N - sum(counts.values())
43:    return {el: c / N for el, c in counts.items()}
44:
45:
46:def e_pure(el, v):
47:    k = (el, round(v, 8))
48:    if k not in _pe:
49:        a = bulk(el, "fcc", a=4.0, cubic=True)
50:        a.set_cell(a.cell * (v * 4 / a.get_volume()) ** (1 / 3), scale_atoms=True)
51:        a.calc = calc
52:        _pe[k] = a.get_potential_energy() / 4
53:    return _pe[k]
54:
55:
56:def ref_err(comp, xa, v):
57:    return sum((xa[e] - comp[e]) * e_pure(e, v) for e in comp)
58:
59:
60:def fix_ev(path):
61:    df = pd.read_csv(path)
62:    out = []
63:    for _, r in df.iterrows():
64:        c = parse_comp(r.comp)
65:        xa = actual(c)
66:        v0 = r.V0
67:        em = np.array([r[f"emix_{i}"] - ref_err(c, xa, v) for i, v in enumerate(v0 * SCALES**3)])
68:        cc, b, a = np.polyfit(np.log(SCALES**3), em, 2)
69:        out.append({**r.to_dict(), "comp_actual": key(xa), "E_mix_logged": r.E_mix, "E_mix": a, "dE_dlnV": b,
70:                    "d2E_dlnV2": 2 * cc, "n_eff": -3 * b / a, **{f"emix_{i}": e for i, e in enumerate(em)}})
71:    o = pd.DataFrame(out)
72:    o.to_csv(path.with_name(path.stem + "_fixed.csv"), index=False)
73:    return o
74:
75:
76:def fix_v0(df):
77:    rows = []
78:    for _, r in df.iterrows():
79:        c = parse_comp(r.comp)
80:        xa = actual(c)
81:        rows.append({**r.to_dict(), "comp_actual": key(xa), "E_mix_logged": r.E_mix,
82:                     "E_mix": r.E_mix - ref_err(c, xa, r.V0)})
83:    return pd.DataFrame(rows)
84:
85:
86:for f in ("h1_ev_rows.csv", "h3_fresh_rows.csv"):
87:    o = fix_ev(ROOT / "data" / f)
88:    d = (o.E_mix - o.E_mix_logged) * 1000
89:    print(f, f"rows {len(o)}, correction meV: median |.| {d.abs().median():.1f}, max |.| {d.abs().max():.1f}, "
90:             f"exact rows {(d.abs() < 1e-6).sum()}", flush=True)
91:hf = fix_v0(pd.read_csv(ROOT / "data" / "hm_fresh_rows.csv"))
92:hf.to_csv(ROOT / "data" / "hm_fresh_rows_fixed.csv", index=False)
93:d = (hf.E_mix - hf.E_mix_logged) * 1000
94:print("hm_fresh_rows.csv", f"rows {len(hf)}, correction median |.| {d.abs().median():.1f}, max {d.abs().max():.1f}")
95:
96:# sealed holdout: corrected without being looked at; compositions and V0 are recomputed from the plain comps file
97:sc = pd.read_csv(ROOT / "data" / "sealed" / "hm3_comps.csv")
98:sealed = arena._unseal("hm3").set_index("comp").loc[sc.comp]
99:sc["E_mix"] = sealed.E_mix.values
100:sc["V0"] = sc.comp.map(lambda s: sum(x * pv[e] for e, x in parse_comp(s).items()))
101:fx = fix_v0(sc)
102:tmp = ROOT / "data" / "hm3fix_tmp.csv"
103:fx[["comp", "comp_actual", "n_el", "E_mix"]].to_csv(tmp, index=False)

106:    ROOT / "data" / "sealed" / "hm3fix_comps.csv", index=False)
107:print("hm3 sealed copy corrected (values not printed)")

1:"""L3 gate: does a correction term found on ML data hold on independent DFT or experiment?
2:
3:The term's functional form and its coefficient are both fixed on the training (ML) set.
4:Within each dataset the baseline is built from that dataset's own pure element values,
5:so a method-wide bias (e.g. MACE shear softening) cancels to first order in the residual.
6:"""
7:
8:from __future__ import annotations
9:
10:import numpy as np
11:import pandas as pd
12:from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
13:
14:from harness.discover import library
15:
16:MIN_TEST = 15
17:
18:
19:def term_values(df: pd.DataFrame, term: str) -> np.ndarray:
20:    cols = sorted(set(term.split("*")))
21:    return library(df, cols)[term].to_numpy()
22:
23:
24:def fit(x: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray) -> LinearRegression:
25:    return LinearRegression().fit(x.reshape(-1, 1), y)
26:
27:
28:def l3_check(train: pd.DataFrame, test: pd.DataFrame, target: str, baseline: str, term: str,
29:             group: str, n_boot: int = 2000, seed: int = 0) -> dict:
30:    ytr = (train[target] - train[baseline]).to_numpy()
31:    yte = (test[target] - test[baseline]).to_numpy()
32:    xtr, xte = term_values(train, term), term_values(test, term)
33:    m_tr = fit(xtr, ytr)
34:    rmse = lambda r: float(np.sqrt(np.mean(r**2)))  # noqa: E731
35:    base = rmse(yte - ytr.mean())  # intercept-only transfer: best a term-free correction can do
36:    transfer = rmse(yte - m_tr.predict(xte.reshape(-1, 1)))
37:    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
38:    boot = []
39:    for _ in range(n_boot):
40:        i = rng.integers(0, len(yte), len(yte))
41:        if np.ptp(xte[i]) > 0:
42:            boot.append(fit(xte[i], yte[i]).coef_[0])
43:    lo, hi = np.percentile(boot, [2.5, 97.5])
44:    c_tr, c_te = float(m_tr.coef_[0]), float(fit(xte, yte).coef_[0])
45:    overlap = sorted(set(train[group]) & set(test[group]))
46:    out = {"term": term, "target": target, "n_train": len(train), "n_test": len(test),
47:           "test_rmse_intercept_only": base, "test_rmse_transfer": transfer,
48:           "gain_transfer": 1 - transfer / base, "coef_train": c_tr, "coef_test": c_te,
49:           "coef_test_ci95": (float(lo), float(hi)), "family_overlap": overlap}
50:    out["passes_L3"] = bool(
51:        not overlap and len(test) >= MIN_TEST and out["gain_transfer"] > 0.1
52:        and (lo > 0 or hi < 0) and np.sign(c_te) == np.sign(c_tr) and 0.5 <= c_te / c_tr <= 2)
53:    return out

# Binary shear curvatures transfer to multicomponent fcc alloys at the alloy's volume: a blind, preregistered test with machine-learned potentials

Muhammet Can Ergani?
Independent researcher, METU graduate, Ankara, T?rkiye. ORCID 0009-0001-1397-6366

Draft v2, 2026-11-01. Every number cites a ledger id in `claims/claims.jsonl`. Items marked TODO block submission.

## Abstract

Pair-additive extrapolation from binaries (regular solution, Muggianu, Redlich-Kister) is the default way to estimate
properties of high-entropy alloys, and it works poorly for shear elastic constants. We show that for the clamped
mixing part of the tetragonal shear curvature K' of random fcc alloys most of the failure is a volume mismatch: each
50:50 binary curvature has to be read at the multicomponent alloy's Vegard volume, not at the binary's own. With no
fitted parameter, the pair sum then predicts K'_mix of 3 to 5 component alloys of Ag, Au, Co, Cu, Ir, Ni, Pd, Pt, Rh
with half the error of the same sum at the binaries' own volumes (4.2 to 1.9 GPa on 94 blind alloys; 4.8 to 2.2 GPa
on 1200 more under a second model) and a third of the error of standard own-volume Muggianu extrapolation (5.7 to
1.9 GPa). The transfer is not exact: the refit slope is 1.08 under one model and 1.14 [1.10, 1.18] under another, and
it grows with size mismatch, so the rule under-predicts alloys with large volume differences between components. For
the C44-type shear K44 the same rule is weak, and we show that the reason is a composition-level residual shared by
both shears that survives separate cells, separate seeds and removal of the clamped pre-stress. All tests were
registered with measured power in an append-only ledger before their data existed, and every pass was audited by an
agent that did not propose it. All targets come from universal machine-learned potentials (MACE); first-principles
validation is pending and is the main limit of this work.

## 1. Introduction

1. HEA screening uses binary data. CALPHAD elastic databases fit Redlich-Kister parameters to the c_ij of relaxed
   SQS, each at its own equilibrium volume (Liu et al. 2010; Marker et al. 2017, bcc Ti-Mo-Nb-Sn-Ta-Zr, Young's
   modulus of 13 alloys within 5 to 7 GPa of experiment). Others average binary moduli (Huhn et al. 2014) or train ML
   models on binaries for Ni-Cu-Au-Pd-Pt (Linton and Aidhy 2023; Mirzaee et al. 2024). Shear transfers worse than
   bulk in all of them and C44 worst; none explains why.
2. Volume-dependent interactions are old: volume-dependent ECIs (Asta et al. 1992; Geng et al. 2005), the alloy-volume
   formalism for binaries (Ferreira, Mbaye, Zunger 1987-89), strain-dependent cluster expansion (Behara et al. 2023).
   They are used for energies and bulk moduli, not for shear, and not as a binary-to-multicomponent transfer rule.
3. Formally the rule is a pair-truncated tensorial cluster expansion (van de Walle 2008) or a zeroth-order
   Redlich-Kister sum. The contribution is not the algebra. It is (i) where the binary terms must be evaluated, (ii) a
   blind preregistered test of that choice, (iii) where it stops working, and (iv) why the C44-type shear behaves
   differently. A similar lesson holds in ML for diffraction, where changing the prediction target, not the model,
   cut errors several fold (Hofgard et al., Acta Cryst. A, 2026, TODO exact reference): here the binary data are
   unchanged and only the volume at which they are read changes.

## 2. Methods

**Cells.** Random fcc solid solutions, 108-atom cubic supercells (3x3x3), atoms on ideal sites (no ionic or cell
relaxation), volume fixed at the composition's Vegard volume V0 from the model's pure-element volumes.

**Observable.** E_mix(V, F) = E_alloy - sum x_i E_i, every pure reference at the same volume and the same deformation
F. K' from F = diag(e^t, e^-t, 1), K44 from F = I + g e_x e_y, five amplitudes in [-0.01, 0.01], quadratic fit,
K' = c2/(2V), K44 = 2 c2/V. References use the cell's actual (integer-count) fractions. At V0 a clamped cell is not
stress free, so K44 = C44 + s_yy and K' = C' + (s_xx + s_yy)/2; Section 3.6 removes this term explicitly.

**Binary inputs.** All 36 pairs at 50:50, three SQS seeds per panel, 13 log-volume points ln(V/V_ij) in [-0.4, 0.4],
cubic spline per pair.

**Rule.** K'_mix(alloy) = sum_{i<j} 4 x_i x_j K'_ij(ln V0/V_ij). Baselines: the same sum at ln V0/V_ij = 0, and
own-volume Muggianu (pure-element K'(V) at their own volumes, converted to the clamped reference).

**Seeds.** The site permutation of a cell depends only on (seed, n). Target cells and input cells (binaries,
references) therefore never share a seed: targets use seeds of 100 and above, binaries 0 to 25. An earlier test that
broke this rule was withdrawn before its targets were read (Section 4).

**Models.** MACE medium-omat-0, calibrated on 14 cubic metals (fcc B, G MAE about 12%, e5ef5a57a3). Second model:
medium-mpa-0, with omat geometry (V_ij, V0) so that only the energies change.

**Protocol.** Hypotheses come from two LLM agents (GPT-6-Astra via Codex, Claude Opus) who see the problem, the
limits and the data, never sealed holdouts. Before any test datum exists the harness owner writes the claim, the
pass criterion and a simulated power (>= 0.8) and false-pass rate (<= 0.05) to the ledger. A failed test is closed
with a cause (hypothesis, design, numerics) after an independent audit; only "hypothesis" retires a candidate. Every
pass is audited by the model that did not propose it, which recomputes the key numbers from the raw files.

**Statistics.** Gain = 1 - RMSE(rule)/RMSE(baseline); paired sign-flip test on squared-error differences; refit slope
k from (y - base) = k (rule - base). With two independent binary panels A and B the slope is estimated cross-panel,
k = sum[T_A (y - p_B) + T_B (y - p_A)] / (2 sum T_A T_B), so binary noise does not bias it; CIs bootstrap over
compositions and over seeds within each panel.

## 3. Results

**3.1 Exploration.** On 62 ternary to quinary alloys used for exploration (a2): K' pair sum 5.67 to rule 1.80 GPa,
k 1.05.

**3.2 Blind test 1 (h3, 113 alloys, prereg 4c29d9754c).** K': 4.77 to 2.03 GPa, gain 0.57, p 2.5e-4, k 1.08. The
registered claim was joint (K44 and K'); it failed on K44 (p 0.023, 6e0923b413), so K' got a fresh test rather than a
post-hoc split.

**3.3 Blind test 2 (hm_fresh, 94 alloys never computed, prereg 67a358fc59).** K': 4.22 to 1.89 GPa, gain 0.55,
p 2.5e-4, k 1.08, rule better in 75 of 94 alloys (d92844787f, L2 697c2d6d75).

**3.4 Against the standard method.** Own-volume Muggianu, the clamped analogue of the CALPHAD c_ij practice (Marker
et al. 2017: every input at its own volume, no volume dependence in the interaction parameters): 5.45 / 5.71 / 5.41
GPa on h3 / hm_fresh / a2; rule 2.03 / 1.89 / 1.94 (p 5e-5). For the mixing energy the same comparison shows no gain
(13.3 vs 11.5 meV): there the volume term is mostly the reference strain energy, which the standard reference already
removes. K' is different because the binary curvatures themselves change steeply with volume (median dlnK'/dlnV =
-3.2 for pairs with |K'| > 10 GPa).

**3.5 Second model, and the size of k (prereg 88b9465108, result 43370bbb27, verdict 736bcac471).** Under
medium-mpa-0, on 1200 new compositions (Co yes/no x 3/4/5 elements, 200 each, two cells each) with two independent
binary panels, the rule cuts the RMSE from 4.81 to 2.21 GPa (gain 0.54) and wins in 934 of 1200 alloys. The
preregistered equivalence claim k in [0.90, 1.10] failed: k = 1.138, 90% CI [1.098, 1.182]. The audit found no coding
error; all 3+3 panel splits give 1.138 to 1.139. The slope is not a constant. Exploratory splits (not preregistered):
3-component 1.00 [0.91, 1.09], 4-component 1.25, 5-component 1.17; Cu-free 1.00 [0.94, 1.07], Cu-containing 1.24;
alloys whose largest pair |ln V0/V_ij| is at most 0.15 give 1.07, above 0.25 give 1.41. Co content does not matter
(1.137 vs 1.139). Under omat, cells of Section 3.6 give k 1.11 [1.02, 1.20] with the same stratification. We read
this as an under-prediction at large size mismatch: the pair transfer captures most of the volume effect but not all
of it. A refit k adds only 3% over k = 1, so the parameter-free rule remains the practical form.

**3.6 The C44-type shear.** The same rule is weak for K44 (leak-free gain 0.06 to 0.14). Three preregistered tests
show why: K44 and K' share a residual that belongs to the composition, not to the cell or the noise.
- Shared floor, disjoint seeds (150 new alloys, half with Co >= 15%; prereg c2eff007ad, result b86e0d8a40): the
  difference A = K44 - K' follows the rule (gain 0.49), the residuals of the two shears correlate (r 0.77), and a joint
  fit gives k 0.91 and floor slope b 0.94. Plain K44 gains 0.47 in Co-free alloys and 0.09 in Co alloys.
- Two cells per composition with seeds unique to each cell (prereg fd786169e3): the K44 residual of one cell
  correlates with the K' residual of the other (r 0.75; same cell 0.79), k 0.92, b 0.95.
- After subtracting the clamped mixing pre-stress from targets and binaries alike (prereg ede47f1d65): cross-cell
  r 0.67, k 0.99, b 0.79. The pre-stress is large (7 GPa rms) but pair-additive (the rule leaves 0.7 GPa of it), so
  it was never the floor.
So K44 = rule44 + b (K' - rule') with b near 1: the C44-type shear fails because it carries a composition floor that
K' also carries, while its own volume signal is about half as large. Open doubt (audit of ede47f1d65): b drops to 0.4
to 0.5 when single disjoint binary seeds are used, so part of the floor may be error shared through the binary
references. TODO: two independent binary panels for K44, K' and stress.

## 4. What the audits caught

The loop's most useful outputs were errors, each found by the agent that did not write the code and confirmed by the
other.

| Error | Found by | Size | What it changed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Integer-count reference mismatch | audit | up to 57 meV/atom | all mixing quantities recomputed |
| PBE cutoff mismatch between alloy and pure references | audit | (TODO size) | rule added: references use the alloy cutoff |
| Holdout used for model selection | audit, d26bd71285 | (TODO) | holdout sealed, targets shuffled |
| Shared SQS permutation between targets and binaries (seed 0) | S2 audit, Opus, confirmed by Astra | K44 Co-free gain inflated | test withdrawn (42c0fd3ee0) before reading, seeds separated |
| Weak baseline made a known energy rule look new | audit | 13.3 vs 11.5 meV | energy rule demoted |
| Power simulation treated a compositional residual as cell noise | audit of 88b9465108 | power 1.0 reported | lesson: simulate residuals at composition level |
| PBE runs with nspin 1 still magnetize Co and Ni | Astra, S3 | not used in any result | Co/Ni PBE blocked until fixed |

## 5. Discussion and limits

1. Model only. Every target is a MACE energy. The slope already differs between two MACE models (1.08, 1.14), and in
   a small set of ordered L1_2 A3B cells (preliminary, unaudited) MACE gets the sign of K44 wrong where PBE gives
   -32 GPa (Au3Ir). K' agreed better. Only PBE on random alloys decides how much of the rule is physical. TODO: PBE
   SQS check on 10 to 15 alloys.
2. Clamped, unrelaxed cells: K'_mix is not the measured C'. On 43 seen equiatomic ternaries with fully relaxed MACE
   constants, own-volume Muggianu of relaxed binaries already reaches 3.1 GPa for C' and a chain built on the volume
   rule 2.5 GPa (gain 0.18, p 0.08, exploratory). At zero pressure the advantage is small and not yet significant.
3. The rule under-predicts at large size mismatch (Section 3.5). A correction for this has not been tested.
4. fcc late transition and noble metals only; bcc shear fails calibration for every model available.
5. The rule is a regular-solution / tensorial-CE truncation with a specified volume; we do not claim a new law.
